current.text: He has been traded to Toronto, where he takes Brandon Ingram's spot.
He faces no punishment from the league ruling.
He is a projected starter next to Quickley, Barrett, Barnes and Poeltl, and he is in the expected closing five.

Plenty of Toronto's offense is expected to run through him, with usage moving to him and away from Barrett and Quickley. His numbers should stay similar to his Clippers numbers apart from normal age decline.
He is coming off one of his best and healthiest seasons in years.
Experts project him as a top 10 per-game player. His per-game range is tight: best case 4th, worst case 21st.
He is expected to miss time. One expert projects about 60 to 65 games.
The Raptors have 15 back-to-backs, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.
Experts disagree on back-to-backs. Some expect him to play some but not all, one expects him to play most unless he gets hurt, and one expects load management in Toronto.
Do not draft him inside the top 40 in head-to-head because of his knee. He becomes a fair pick around 41 to 45, or in round 4 or 5.
Experts say his market price is too high when he goes around picks 20 to 29.
In an auction, one expert would pay no more than 24 USD for him. He went for 20 USD in that mock.

durable.text: He has a degenerative knee condition with repeated surgeries in the same knee (meniscus, ACL, quad tendinopathy). He also carries ankle sprain risk.
Experts do not trust his knee to hold up. Their main worry is injuries and load management.
He is a high-usage player, with over 30 percent usage last season.
He is a good and willing three-point shooter and one of the best free throw shooters in recent memory. He makes decisions quickly.
Steals are his standout category, far above the pool. Points and FT% are also clearly strong, and no category is weak.
Because he misses games, he is worth a bit more in roto than in head-to-head.

note: Per game he fits any build: 1.7 steals, 24.7 points, 88 percent FT on 5 attempts and no weak category. His knee and expected rest days make games the real question, and the Raptors have three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks. The ESPN value of 40 USD is too high. Stay near the expert cap of 24 USD, which fits his 20 USD price in our league last season and his 27.9 USD Yahoo average cost. Early in the season, check how many back-to-backs he plays and whether he gets any new knee news.
